newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds outperform, spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds outperform, spreads narrow.

text.p: Australian bond spreads narrowed as the local market outperformed other markets on well-received testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the outlook for the U.S. economy.
Bonds did not reverse all the widening that occured on Tuesday, when the local market sold off on profit taking and book squaring ahead of the Greenspan testimony.
However, bonds still closed near 80 points over U.S. long bonds, well down on last week's levels, and a sign of the underlying positive tone to local markets, traders said.

Traders expect local bonds to remain well supported ahead of next Wednesday's December quarter CPI, although due to a lack of near term local leads the market is expected to track the Treasuries market through the rest of this week.
Long bonds continued their stronger tone of the last week or so, although the curves are still slightly steeper than Monday's closing levels.

The 100 point spread on the futures on Wednesday was seven points flatter than just over one week ago, and traders said in a bullish market the long end had the best potential given some emerging doubts over the possibility of a fourth rate cut.
